questions.question: Why isn't temporary generation equivalent to permanent firm power?
options: Battery storage supplies indefinite firm power without replenishment
Once equipment is energized, its permit duration no longer affects availability
Nameplate turbine output proves uninterrupted long-term delivery
Permits, fuel, reliability, and operating duration can limit it
questions.correct_answer: Permits, fuel, reliability, and operating duration can limit it
questions.why: Getting a cluster online quickly and sustaining it reliably are different accomplishments.

questions.question: Why should a reported 122-day deployment and a 19-day installation milestone not be treated as contradictory?
options: Both figures necessarily measure groundbreaking to full commercial utilization
The shorter figure proves every prerequisite was completed in that same period
They can measure different start points in the same deployment
The shorter figure measures the entire project and the longer one only rack installation
questions.correct_answer: They can measure different start points in the same deployment
questions.why: NVIDIA reported 122 days for the supporting facility and system, and 19 days from first rack to training.

questions.question: How do megawatts and gigawatts relate?
options: A gigawatt measures energy while a megawatt measures power
One megawatt equals 1,000 gigawatts
One gigawatt equals 1,000 megawatts
One gigawatt equals 100 megawatts
questions.correct_answer: One gigawatt equals 1,000 megawatts
questions.why: Both are units of power; the prefix changes the scale.

questions.question: What is the supplier-competitor or frenemy problem?
options: A supplier agrees never to develop any model
Two companies use the same accounting software
A customer buys from several suppliers that never compete with it
A firm provides infrastructure while also competing in AI products
questions.correct_answer: A firm provides infrastructure while also competing in AI products
questions.why: The relationship can combine mutual benefit with conflicting incentives.

questions.question: What would an outside-capacity purchase by Google show most directly?
options: That Google lacks any internal capacity suitable for AI
That Anthropic’s contracted alternatives have ceased to exist
That the supplier’s current pricing power must persist for the entire contract term
That Google valued the offered capacity on the offered timeline and terms
questions.correct_answer: That Google valued the offered capacity on the offered timeline and terms
questions.why: One deal can validate timely supply without proving universal dependence.

questions.question: Why is reusability alone insufficient to guarantee very low launch costs?
options: Recovering hardware once proves it can be reused cheaply at high frequency
A high design payload guarantees low cost per kilogram at any load factor
Turnaround, refurbishment, reliability, payload, and launch frequency also matter
Reusing a booster removes upper-stage and payload-integration costs
questions.correct_answer: Turnaround, refurbishment, reliability, payload, and launch frequency also matter
questions.why: Economics depend on the whole operating system, not a single recovery demonstration.

questions.question: What is vertical integration?
options: Controlling one bottleneck while outsourcing every other value-chain stage
Buying from multiple vendors to avoid dependence on any one stage
Control of multiple stages of a value chain within one organization
Expanding output at one stage without changing control of other stages
questions.correct_answer: Control of multiple stages of a value chain within one organization
questions.why: Launch, satellite manufacture, and compute services illustrate different stages; integration does not remove all risks.

questions.question: Why does a shortage of NVIDIA GPUs not by itself prove all TPU capacity is unavailable?
options: Different chip architectures guarantee unrelated supply conditions in every respect
Chip contracts eliminate any shared constraints in power, construction, or networking
The resources and commitments overlap only partly and are not identical
A GPU purchase reveals the exact remaining availability of every TPU allocation
questions.correct_answer: The resources and commitments overlap only partly and are not identical
questions.why: Chip-specific scarcity and industry-wide power scarcity must be distinguished.

questions.question: What does a mutual termination right mean?
options: Both parties may exit under the contract's specified conditions
Both parties may exit immediately without complying with notice requirements
Both parties must agree again each time either wants to exercise the right
Only the customer may exit because it pays for the service
questions.correct_answer: Both parties may exit under the contract's specified conditions
questions.why: Mutual describes who holds the right; timing and conditions still matter.

questions.question: Why can a popular, high-quality model still fail to realize all its potential revenue?
options: Strong model quality ensures that capacity automatically expands with demand
Its available serving capacity may not meet user demand
Serving constraints affect costs but cannot limit realized sales
Future contracted capacity is sufficient even before it is delivered
questions.correct_answer: Its available serving capacity may not meet user demand
questions.why: Demand, model quality, and capacity to serve requests are distinct.

questions.question: Which risk remains even if competitors cannot match a company's launch capability?
options: A moat guarantees the required launch cost even if refurbishment remains expensive
An FCC filing transfers performance risk from the company to the regulator
Competition is the only source of risk once the basic concept is proposed
The company may still fail to achieve the required cost, reliability, or cadence
questions.correct_answer: The company may still fail to achieve the required cost, reliability, or cadence
questions.why: Protection from rivals is not protection from physics, engineering, financing, or operating failures.

questions.question: What is margin stacking?
options: The gross profit of one integrated company measured before depreciation
The extra cost caused solely by financing successive construction phases
Successive independent suppliers each adding their own profit margin
The difference between a customer’s revenue and its infrastructure spending
questions.correct_answer: Successive independent suppliers each adding their own profit margin
questions.why: Integration may reduce some external markups but still requires capital and efficient operations.

questions.question: Why does an initial non-cancellable period matter in a deal with 90-day notice rights?
options: It prevents either party from ever terminating before the scheduled final date
It guarantees unchanged pricing even after a valid termination and new negotiation
The notice right may apply only after that protected period
It makes the notice period optional after the customer starts using capacity
questions.correct_answer: The notice right may apply only after that protected period
questions.why: The existence of an exit clause does not tell you when it becomes exercisable.

questions.question: What is Google's Project Suncatcher exploring?
options: Solar-powered satellite networks for machine-learning compute in space
A plan to run ordinary satellites without any communications links
A replacement for all terrestrial internet traffic already operating commercially
A ground-based solar installation that manufactures CPUs
questions.correct_answer: Solar-powered satellite networks for machine-learning compute in space
questions.why: Google describes it as a research moonshot, not proven commercial-scale infrastructure.

questions.question: What is an economic moat?
options: A competitive advantage that can make entry or imitation difficult
A first-mover lead that guarantees permanent market power
A large capital budget independent of execution or barriers to entry
A high current profit margin even when entry is easy
questions.correct_answer: A competitive advantage that can make entry or imitation difficult
questions.why: Barriers such as expertise, capital, infrastructure, and operating experience can support a moat.

questions.question: What is a stock lock-up expiration?
options: The end of restrictions on sales by specified holders
An automatic issue of new shares by the company
The point at which insiders must sell their eligible shares
The expiry of a customer’s minimum compute commitment
questions.correct_answer: The end of restrictions on sales by specified holders
questions.why: More shares may become eligible for sale, but the price effect is not predetermined.

questions.question: Why are high-bandwidth inter-satellite links important to distributed orbital AI?
options: More satellites eliminate the need for high-performance links between them
Their role is only to downlink final answers and cannot affect distributed computation
Cooperating processors must exchange large amounts of data efficiently
High bandwidth alone removes all formation-control and latency requirements
questions.correct_answer: Cooperating processors must exchange large amounts of data efficiently
questions.why: A collection of accelerators needs networking to work as a useful distributed system.

questions.question: Why can't a single stock-price move identify the market's exact reasoning?
options: The size of a price change reveals the exact weight assigned to each risk
A flat price proves new positive and negative developments were identical in size
Many expectations, risks, and trading forces can move prices simultaneously
A decline after a disclosure proves that disclosure was the sole cause
questions.correct_answer: Many expectations, risks, and trading forces can move prices simultaneously
questions.why: Price action alone is not a controlled test of one explanation.

questions.question: How is an infrastructure-owning hyperscaler different from a model lab that largely buys compute?
options: Its internal capacity is always less costly than external capacity for every workload
It controls all relevant power and hardware supply and therefore has no counterparty risk
It controls more of its own physical supply and investment pipeline
It only provides infrastructure and cannot compete in AI models
questions.correct_answer: It controls more of its own physical supply and investment pipeline
questions.why: Ownership changes options and risks without eliminating bottlenecks.

questions.question: What is redundancy intended to improve?
options: Reduced need for maintenance through a larger primary power feed
Resilience when equipment or a power path fails
Higher productive utilization under every workload
Lower construction time by eliminating backup equipment
questions.correct_answer: Resilience when equipment or a power path fails
questions.why: Backup paths and equipment reduce single-point failures, often at added cost and time.

questions.question: Why can faster time-to-online create economic value during scarcity?
options: Faster construction permanently protects the supplier from lower rental prices
Earlier online capacity guarantees higher returns even if utilization is low
Useful capacity can earn revenue or run workloads sooner
Speed creates value only when the company uses the capacity internally
questions.correct_answer: Useful capacity can earn revenue or run workloads sooner
questions.why: Earlier availability has value when customers would otherwise wait.

questions.question: What is the careful meaning of an asymmetric opportunity here?
options: Large potential upside if execution succeeds, alongside meaningful concentrated downside
A market lead limits downside while leaving all upside uncapped
A large upside proves that the probability-weighted return is attractive
A technically feasible project cannot have concentrated financial losses
questions.correct_answer: Large potential upside if execution succeeds, alongside meaningful concentrated downside
questions.why: Asymmetry describes possible outcomes, not a conclusion that the bet is safe or attractively priced.

questions.question: What is the key caution about an annualized monthly revenue run rate?
options: Multiplying one month by twelve is not the same as revenue actually earned over a year
An annualized month is equivalent to a full year of recognized revenue
A monthly revenue run rate automatically represents non-cancellable recurring contracts
Annualizing a high-growth month establishes the next year’s cash collections
questions.correct_answer: Multiplying one month by twelve is not the same as revenue actually earned over a year
questions.why: A snapshot extrapolation depends on whether the monthly level persists; it is not automatically contracted recurring revenue either.

questions.question: Why is vacuum cooling a challenge rather than an automatic benefit?
options: Cold surroundings remove heat without requiring sufficient radiator area
Vacuum improves ordinary air-cooled heat sinks by increasing convection
There is no ambient air for convection, so heat must ultimately be radiated away
Thermal management matters during launch but not after stable orbit is reached
questions.correct_answer: There is no ambient air for convection, so heat must ultimately be radiated away
questions.why: Radiators and thermal pathways are essential even with a cold space background.

questions.question: How do spot rates differ from prices fixed in an existing contract?
options: Spot rates reflect current market terms; contract prices follow the agreement
A rising spot rate automatically raises every fixed contract fee
Contract prices become spot prices whenever the supplier has a waiting list
Spot rates are the average price across every existing long-term contract
questions.correct_answer: Spot rates reflect current market terms; contract prices follow the agreement
questions.why: A changed market can affect renewal or new deals without automatically rewriting existing terms.

questions.question: What is bridge capacity?
options: An emergency purchase that cannot have a multi-year contractual end date
Temporary external capacity covering a gap while longer-term supply catches up
Permanent replacement for the buyer’s own infrastructure strategy
Capacity already owned internally but temporarily unused
questions.correct_answer: Temporary external capacity covering a gap while longer-term supply catches up
questions.why: Bridge purchases address timing mismatches rather than necessarily replacing a long-term strategy.

questions.question: What does a pro-rata fee reduction do when less capacity is delivered?
options: Adjusts the fee in proportion to the relevant delivered quantity
Keeps the full contracted fee while shortening the contract term proportionally
Reduces the fee by a fixed amount independent of delivered capacity
Requires immediate termination rather than permitting reduced service
questions.correct_answer: Adjusts the fee in proportion to the relevant delivered quantity
questions.why: Delivery remedies can distinguish paying for partial service from terminating it.

questions.question: How should a claim that a customer has no choice be tested?
options: A mutual notice clause proves both parties have equally good alternatives
A list of supplier names proves immediate equivalent replacement capacity
Examine workable substitutes, timing, contractual rights, and switching costs
A large contract demonstrates unlimited pricing power for its entire life
questions.correct_answer: Examine workable substitutes, timing, contractual rights, and switching costs
questions.why: The discussion itself distinguishes constrained alternatives from literally no alternatives.

questions.question: What is a binding constraint?
options: The contractual obligation with the longest remaining term
The bottleneck currently limiting an achievable outcome
The largest cost item, whether or not it limits output
The slowest resource to expand, even when there is surplus available
questions.correct_answer: The bottleneck currently limiting an achievable outcome
questions.why: If usable compute is the bottleneck, better demand alone cannot remove it.

questions.question: What is launch cadence?
options: How frequently launches can be performed
The time required for one launch to reach orbit
The percentage of launched satellites that become operational
The payload mass carried per launch
questions.correct_answer: How frequently launches can be performed
questions.why: High frequency must be operationally sustainable, not just an announced target.

questions.question: How can scarce capacity strengthen a supplier's bargaining position?
options: Customers may find equivalent timely alternatives difficult to obtain
Scarcity removes the supplier’s own incentive to retain major customers
Scarcity automatically rewrites the price of existing non-cancellable service
A shortage proves the customer has no alternatives at any price or timeline
questions.correct_answer: Customers may find equivalent timely alternatives difficult to obtain
questions.why: Leverage depends on outside options and timing, not an unlimited legal right to reprice.

questions.question: Why is multi-provider diversification useful but incomplete protection?
options: It guarantees equivalent performance across vendors without software changes
It reduces single-supplier exposure without ensuring instant equivalent replacement
It removes shared power bottlenecks because different suppliers have different names
It ensures contracted future capacity can replace current service immediately
questions.correct_answer: It reduces single-supplier exposure without ensuring instant equivalent replacement
questions.why: Diversification reduces some risks while shared bottlenecks and switching costs remain.

questions.question: Which sequence best separates stages of a data-center project?
options: Contracted capacity, then full utilization, then power connection
Installed, energized, and fully used capacity are equivalent if chips are present
Planned and contracted capacity are equivalent once financing is announced
Planned, contracted, installed, energized, then productively used capacity
questions.correct_answer: Planned, contracted, installed, energized, then productively used capacity
questions.why: Physical completion, power availability, contracts, and actual use must not be conflated.

questions.question: How does an IPO price differ from a later market price?
options: The IPO price is an audited estimate of intrinsic business value
IPO pricing sets the offering price; later trading reflects subsequent bids and offers
A later price near the IPO price means no new information has arrived
The IPO price guarantees later investors pay for the same expectations
questions.correct_answer: IPO pricing sets the offering price; later trading reflects subsequent bids and offers
questions.why: Neither price alone proves whether a business is fairly valued.

questions.question: How should a roughly $200-per-kilogram launch benchmark be used?
options: As an assumption-dependent research scenario, not a universal break-even guarantee
As proof that launch cost is the only remaining orbital-compute expense
As an observed market-wide price already available for sustained deployment
As a universal cost-parity threshold independent of mission assumptions
questions.correct_answer: As an assumption-dependent research scenario, not a universal break-even guarantee
questions.why: Full economics also depend on hardware, lifetime, thermal systems, utilization, and other costs.

questions.question: Why doesn't agreement between a chatbot and a video independently verify a claim?
options: Both may rely on the same source or repeat the same unsupported assumption
Two agreeing summaries are independent if they use different wording
Agreement is sufficient unless another commentator explicitly disputes the claim
A confident chatbot assessment counts as verification of the video it summarizes
questions.correct_answer: Both may rely on the same source or repeat the same unsupported assumption
questions.why: Source independence and primary evidence matter more than repeated confidence.

questions.question: Why is a gigawatt figure alone insufficient to compare two AI clusters?
options: Equal power implies equal throughput when both clusters are called AI data centers
Power alone is enough if the companies publish the same utilization target
Equal power implies equal GPU counts even across different generations
Chip efficiency, networking, workload, and utilization also matter
questions.correct_answer: Chip efficiency, networking, workload, and utilization also matter
questions.why: A GW measures power, not a fixed quantity of AI work.

questions.question: What does an FCC application establish most directly?
options: Independent certification that the proposed system is technically and financially viable
Proof that all manufacturing and launch capacity has already been secured
That an applicant is requesting regulatory authority for a specified system
Regulatory authorization for the complete proposed constellation
questions.correct_answer: That an applicant is requesting regulatory authority for a specified system
questions.why: Application, authorization, deployment, and commercial success are separate stages.

questions.question: Why is a claimed short payback period not guaranteed lifetime profitability?
options: Payback includes all future financing costs and hardware replacements by definition
It depends on assumptions about cash flows, utilization, prices, costs, and asset life
A payback estimate removes sensitivity to future rental prices after the first year
An initial payback claim proves the same returns on later expansion phases
questions.correct_answer: It depends on assumptions about cash flows, utilization, prices, costs, and asset life
questions.why: A simple payback claim omits important parts of a full investment analysis.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a target from a realized result?
options: A target is an intended future outcome; a result is an observed outcome with evidence
A contract’s maximum potential value is recognized revenue at signing
A planned power connection counts as fully utilized capacity once approved
A management target becomes a realized result once financing is arranged
questions.correct_answer: A target is an intended future outcome; a result is an observed outcome with evidence
questions.why: Attribution, dates, and measurement definitions keep forecasts from being remembered as accomplished facts.

questions.question: What is a retrofit advantage in the discussion?
options: Reusing a shell means all power capacity is already secured
A retrofit has no commissioning or cooling-design requirements
A retrofit and a greenfield project have identical permitting prerequisites
Reusing an existing industrial shell can shorten parts of deployment
questions.correct_answer: Reusing an existing industrial shell can shorten parts of deployment
questions.why: Existing buildings can save time without solving every infrastructure requirement.

questions.question: Which summary best preserves the discussion's central distinction?
options: Long-term orbital targets should be valued as delivered capacity once formally filed
Near-term ground capacity may have value while orbital upside remains conditional on execution and economics
Ground build speed proves that large orbital clusters are only a volume problem
A launch moat makes commercial orbital computing inevitable at any cost
questions.correct_answer: Near-term ground capacity may have value while orbital upside remains conditional on execution and economics
questions.why: The near-term business, long-term opportunity, and different kinds of risk should be assessed separately.

questions.question: Why might a hyperscaler buy outside compute despite owning substantial infrastructure?
options: External purchases always mean the buyer lacks its own accelerator technology
A particular chip type, location, or delivery window may be scarce
Buying externally proves internal infrastructure is no longer economically useful
Total owned capacity is sufficient to rule out any short-term resource mismatch
questions.correct_answer: A particular chip type, location, or delivery window may be scarce
questions.why: Aggregate size does not guarantee the right resource is available at the right time.

questions.question: How does a scaling risk differ from an unresolved technology-and-operations risk?
options: Any system that has flown once is beyond technology-and-operations risk
A working subsystem proves the integrated commercial system only needs more copies
Manufacturing scale eliminates the need to verify high-cadence operational reliability
Scaling expands a working system; unresolved risks concern whether required performance can be achieved reliably
questions.correct_answer: Scaling expands a working system; unresolved risks concern whether required performance can be achieved reliably
questions.why: A promising component does not establish the cost and reliability of the fully integrated system.

questions.question: Why distinguish Falcon 9 rideshare from Starship in discussing a prototype launch?
options: A rideshare mission is not an actual orbital launch
A small prototype can be launched only by Starship
A test launched on one vehicle does not demonstrate the other's cost or cadence
All SpaceX launch vehicles have identical payload capacity
questions.correct_answer: A test launched on one vehicle does not demonstrate the other's cost or cadence
questions.why: The discussion's prototype and the proposed large-scale deployment system involve different launch roles.

questions.question: What is a grid-interconnection bottleneck?
options: The period needed to connect individual GPUs through the cluster network
The period needed to commission cooling equipment after power is available
A shortage of chips even when ample electrical service is already secured
A delay in securing the electrical connection and upgrades needed for service
questions.correct_answer: A delay in securing the electrical connection and upgrades needed for service
questions.why: A building can be ready before enough grid power is available.

questions.question: What is optionality in the capacity discussion?
options: An obligation to preserve the same allocation until the hardware is retired
The ability to choose among leasing, internal use, or other permitted allocations
The expected profit of one fixed allocation with no right to change it
A guarantee that internal use will always outperform external leasing
questions.correct_answer: The ability to choose among leasing, internal use, or other permitted allocations
questions.why: Flexibility can have value as demand and internal needs change.

questions.question: Does renting compute necessarily transfer ownership of a customer's model or data?
options: No; ownership and permitted use depend on contractual terms
Yes; renting servers is legally the same as selling all intellectual property
No; contracts can never address data or intellectual property
Yes; whoever owns the GPU always owns every output and model
questions.correct_answer: No; ownership and permitted use depend on contractual terms
questions.why: Infrastructure access and intellectual-property ownership are separate issues.

questions.question: Why isn't a strong competitive lead the same as a proven monopoly for the next decade?
options: Potential entrants are irrelevant until they have already matched current launch cadence
A lead in launch automatically establishes monopoly in AI models and cloud computing
Market definition, substitutes, entrants, and future performance still matter
A large current share proves there are no substitutes for any customer
questions.correct_answer: Market definition, substitutes, entrants, and future performance still matter
questions.why: Dominance in a particular capability does not prove permanent or economy-wide monopoly power.

questions.question: What is meant by terrestrial compute as a cash-flow bridge to orbital ambitions?
options: Proof that booked terrestrial revenue is fully available as free cash flow
Ground operations might generate funds while a riskier orbital system is developed
An assured funding source that makes further financing unnecessary
A requirement that all ground compute be replaced by orbital compute immediately
questions.correct_answer: Ground operations might generate funds while a riskier orbital system is developed
questions.why: It is a proposed funding mechanism, contingent on actual cash generation and competing demands for capital.

questions.question: How can large fixed spending commitments become dangerous?
options: Large commitments are dangerous only if they are already recognized as debt
High fixed spending cannot pressure finances while reported revenue is growing
Unused capacity obligations disappear automatically when the customer forecasts less demand
Payments can remain due even if revenue growth disappoints
questions.correct_answer: Payments can remain due even if revenue growth disappoints
questions.why: Obligations can amplify financial pressure when business forecasts miss.

questions.question: What could weaken today's scarcity-driven rental returns?
options: All existing chips become more expensive to manufacture
More customers seek the same fixed supply
Power shortages delay all competing projects indefinitely
Competing capacity grows faster than demand and rental prices fall
questions.correct_answer: Competing capacity grows faster than demand and rental prices fall
questions.why: Today's attractive pricing is not automatically a durable return forecast.

questions.question: Why test AI accelerators for radiation effects?
options: A total-dose test proves immunity to every single-particle error mechanism
Passing ground radiation tests establishes complete in-orbit mission reliability
Particles can cause errors or degradation that affect reliable computation
Radiation hardening only changes satellite lifetime, not correctness of computation
questions.correct_answer: Particles can cause errors or degradation that affect reliable computation
questions.why: Survival and error behavior both matter; ground tests do not prove every mission condition.

questions.question: What is counterparty risk in a compute arrangement?
options: The risk that chip performance improves faster than expected
The risk that electricity costs rise despite both parties honoring their commitments
The risk that a workload runs inefficiently even when the supplier performs fully
Risk that the other party fails to perform or exercises rights that disrupt plans
questions.correct_answer: Risk that the other party fails to perform or exercises rights that disrupt plans
questions.why: Dependence on another business introduces delivery and relationship risks.

questions.question: What does a learning curve describe in this context?
options: How unit cost may decline as cumulative production and operating experience increase
A forecast of lower unit cost that is already an observed operating result
A guaranteed cost reduction for each additional year, regardless of production
A cost decline that continues at the same rate without any achievable floor
questions.correct_answer: How unit cost may decline as cumulative production and operating experience increase
questions.why: Learning can reduce cost, but the rate and achievable floor must be demonstrated.

questions.question: Which assessment of community opposition is most careful?
options: Assume opposition is irrational whenever a project promises tax revenue
Treat proposed economic benefits as guaranteed outcomes
Assume dry cooling eliminates every local impact
Evaluate water, noise, grid, land-use, and benefit claims on evidence
questions.correct_answer: Evaluate water, noise, grid, land-use, and benefit claims on evidence
questions.why: Legitimate costs and benefits require project-specific evidence, not labels for opponents.

questions.question: What is nameplate capacity best understood as?
options: The useful throughput guaranteed for any model at that power level
The portion of installed capacity currently sold to paying customers
The average measured electrical draw during production workloads
Rated or stated capacity, not a measurement of current productive use
questions.correct_answer: Rated or stated capacity, not a measurement of current productive use
questions.why: Nameplate power is not the same as actual draw, utilization, or useful compute throughput.

questions.question: How should the later discussion of Terafab chipmaking ambitions be recalled?
options: As evidence that owning launch removes semiconductor manufacturing risk
As an added vertical-integration proposal whose status and feasibility require separate evidence
As the same demonstrated milestone as operating a small TPU payload in orbit
As proof that the proposed chip process is already operating at commercial yield
questions.correct_answer: As an added vertical-integration proposal whose status and feasibility require separate evidence
questions.why: An ambition to control another supply-chain stage is not proof of working high-volume semiconductor production.

questions.question: What is customer concentration risk for a capacity supplier?
options: A large share of revenue depends on relatively few buyers
A large fraction of the provider’s chips come from one manufacturer
A large fraction of the provider’s facilities are in one region
A large fraction of the provider’s power comes from one grid connection
questions.correct_answer: A large share of revenue depends on relatively few buyers
questions.why: Losing or repricing one large customer can materially affect results.

questions.question: What is the proposed solar-power attraction of suitable orbits?
options: Long sunlight exposure can increase energy collected per panel area
Solar availability alone determines total computing cost per useful workload
All low Earth orbits provide identical sunlight exposure throughout the year
Higher sunlight yield removes the need to pay for panels and power electronics
questions.correct_answer: Long sunlight exposure can increase energy collected per panel area
questions.why: Energy yield depends on orbit and system design; the power system is not free.

questions.question: Why are GPUs, Google TPUs, and AWS Trainium not perfect substitutes?
options: All accelerators have the same software environment but different brand names
Software stacks, workload fit, performance, and availability can differ
Contracting equivalent power across architectures guarantees equivalent workload throughput
Migration is instantaneous once a customer has a multi-vendor contract
questions.correct_answer: Software stacks, workload fit, performance, and availability can differ
questions.why: Architectural diversity can improve resilience but migration is not frictionless.

questions.question: What is capex?
options: The total of current-period operating and financing expenses
Capital expenditure on longer-lived assets such as infrastructure
The amount of future customer revenue contracted for the infrastructure
The depreciation expense charged during the current period
questions.correct_answer: Capital expenditure on longer-lived assets such as infrastructure
questions.why: Large infrastructure investment uses cash and affects returns over time.

questions.question: Why might the same mutual exit clause have unequal practical value to the two sides?
options: The same legal right ensures equal replacement costs for both parties
Mutual notice automatically cancels scarcity-related bargaining advantages
The party receiving payments necessarily holds the stronger outside option
Their alternatives and replacement costs can differ
questions.correct_answer: Their alternatives and replacement costs can differ
questions.why: Legal symmetry does not guarantee economic symmetry.

questions.question: What does a successful small AI workload in orbit establish most directly?
options: That the full satellite lifetime has been verified under actual radiation conditions
That a prototype can sustain data-center-scale workloads continuously
That distributed multi-satellite training is already commercially competitive
Some hardware and software can operate under those test conditions
questions.correct_answer: Some hardware and software can operate under those test conditions
questions.why: A demonstration is evidence of a milestone, not proof of all future operating and economic requirements.

questions.question: What does compute mean in this discussion?
options: The accelerators alone, excluding networking, storage, and software
Processing resources used to train and run AI models
The model weights and datasets, rather than the resources executing workloads
The electricity consumed, regardless of the useful work completed
questions.correct_answer: Processing resources used to train and run AI models
questions.why: Compute includes accelerators and the supporting systems that make AI workloads possible.

questions.question: What does behind-the-meter generation mean here?
options: Generation bought from a utility but priced under a special tariff
Battery storage charged from the grid, regardless of where generation occurs
Any power supply dedicated by contract to a particular customer
Power generated on the customer side of the utility meter
questions.correct_answer: Power generated on the customer side of the utility meter
questions.why: On-site generation can reduce reliance on grid delivery, but still faces costs and regulatory requirements.

questions.question: What are economic rents in the discussion of a launch bottleneck?
options: A guaranteed return equal to the supplier’s spending on scarce equipment
All revenue before deducting capital and operating costs
All payments customers make for leased infrastructure
Returns enabled by scarce or hard-to-replicate capability beyond a competitive baseline
questions.correct_answer: Returns enabled by scarce or hard-to-replicate capability beyond a competitive baseline
questions.why: Control of a valuable bottleneck may support excess returns, but it does not guarantee them.

questions.question: What makes an apples-to-apples build-speed comparison?
options: Use matching chip counts but ignore whether power and networking were ready
Matching project scope, starting point, completion milestone, and power readiness
Compare announced nameplate capacity even when completion milestones differ
Use first-rack arrival for one project and land acquisition for the other
questions.correct_answer: Matching project scope, starting point, completion milestone, and power readiness
questions.why: Retrofits and greenfield sites can face very different prerequisites.

questions.question: What is latency, as distinct from bandwidth?
options: Latency is delay; bandwidth is the rate at which data can be carried
Latency is average workload utilization; bandwidth is maximum chip power
Latency is the data rate; bandwidth is the delay before a message arrives
Low latency guarantees unlimited data transfer capacity
questions.correct_answer: Latency is delay; bandwidth is the rate at which data can be carried
questions.why: Distributed workloads can be sensitive to both communication rate and delay.

questions.question: What is the key difference between training and inference?
options: Training is compute-intensive; inference adds no material capacity requirement
Training builds new model versions; inference only measures their benchmark scores
Training means initial pretraining only; all later weight updates are inference
Training updates a model; inference uses it to produce outputs
questions.correct_answer: Training updates a model; inference uses it to produce outputs
questions.why: Both require compute, but they use it for different stages of a model's life.

questions.question: What is commissioning after a satellite launch?
options: The transition from a test mission to profitable commercial service
Checking and bringing spacecraft and payload systems into service
Receipt of the first radio signal, with no additional checks required
The manufacturing qualification of future satellites on the ground
questions.correct_answer: Checking and bringing spacecraft and payload systems into service
questions.why: Initial contact is not the same milestone as verified payload operation.

questions.question: Why separate information known at an IPO from later disclosures?
options: A higher revenue figure proves the IPO price did not anticipate growth
To distinguish a new development from confirmation of an already-known plan
All later disclosures should be counted as unexpected improvements
A plan becomes new information every time management repeats it
questions.correct_answer: To distinguish a new development from confirmation of an already-known plan
questions.why: A later announcement can add information, confirm expectations, or disappoint them.

questions.question: Why should up-to amounts, minimum commitments, and conditional spending not simply be added as identical obligations?
options: Adding all figures is accurate if they cover different providers, regardless of overlapping terms
They differ in certainty, cancellation rights, and delivery conditions
An up-to ceiling is the same as a guaranteed minimum because both are contract values
Conditional delivery spending must already have been paid when the agreement is announced
questions.correct_answer: They differ in certainty, cancellation rights, and delivery conditions
questions.why: Contract labels and conditions determine what the figures actually represent.

questions.question: What does a launch price expressed in dollars per kilogram compare?
options: The charge per unit payload mass for specified launch conditions
The cost of satellite electrical capacity per kilowatt in orbit
The complete cost per useful unit of AI work over the mission lifetime
The cost of refurbishing one rocket independent of payload mass
questions.correct_answer: The charge per unit payload mass for specified launch conditions
questions.why: Payload destination, load factor, and what costs are included affect the comparison.

questions.question: How do revenue, operating income, and net income differ?
options: High revenue growth establishes profitability even without expense information
They describe sales, profit after operating costs, and profit after further items respectively
Operating income deducts all financing and tax items, while net income does not
Revenue and cash flow are interchangeable, but net income differs
questions.correct_answer: They describe sales, profit after operating costs, and profit after further items respectively
questions.why: Growth in sales does not alone establish profitability or cash generation.
